Documento(s) de cenário:
--- Project Scenario 8.pdf ---
BECS (Book E-Commerce System)
So basically what we're trying to do is get books selling 
online instead of however you guys are doing it now, just a 
simple site where people can come in, look through what's 
available, throw a few books in a cart and check out. Nothing 
crazy, I just want it to actually work and not be a headache 
to keep up with. Right now I think it's all kind of manual or 
scattered and there's no real way for someone to just browse 
and buy without someone in the middle handling it, so that's 
the itch we're trying to scratch here. 
 
Anybody coming to the site should be able to just make an 
account, that's it, no big verification process or anything, 
and once they're in they can search for books and see title, 
author, price, add stuff to their cart and go through 
checkout. Keep the search simple, just matching on the title 
and it has to be exact, nothing fancy like partial matches or 
letting people search by author, that's more than we need 
right now. Some of these people might want to sign up to get 
notified about promotions and deals, so let's call those folks 
members, and they're the ones who can use promo codes when 
they check out. I picture this being pretty bare-bones in 
terms of who can buy what, like one copy of each book per 
order is plenty, we don't need people stacking ten copies of 
the same thing in their cart. 
 
On my side of things, I need a way to manage the inventory, 
basically a login that lets me add new books, edit prices, see 
how much stock I've got, that kind of stuff. I also want the 
system to ping me, like an email or something, whenever a book 
is running low so I don't get caught without stock, unless 
I've told it not to bother for that particular book because 
maybe I'm discontinuing it. And I want to be able to set up 
these percentage-off promotions every now and then and have it 
just email all the members automatically when I create one. 
 
One thing I want to be upfront about, we don't need to 
actually process real credit cards or handle real money 
movement right now, just collect the card number as part of 
the checkout flow and spit out a receipt and keep a log of 
what was purchased, who bought it, when. The real payment 
processing piece is something for way later, not part of this. 
Same with security stuff, I know that sounds bad, but honestly 
for what we need right now I'm not worried about encryption or 
people forgetting passwords or whatever, that's not a 
priority, let's not spend time building password recovery or 
anything like that for now. 
 
There's only going to be one person managing the store, me 
basically, so don't worry about building out roles for 
multiple managers or anything fancy like that, and a manager 
should never also be a regular customer account, those are two 
separate hats. It just needs to run somewhere people can get 
to it through a normal browser, nothing exotic on the 
technical side, just something stable that people in here can 
pull up and use without issues.

Sistema: BECS (Book E-Commerce System)

Resumo executivo: BECS is a browser-based book e-commerce system that replaces manual and fragmented sales activities with a self-service storefront. Customers can create accounts, search the available catalog, add books to a cart, and complete checkout, while the store manager controls inventory, promotions, and notifications. The system enables online purchasing records without implementing real payment processing.

Escopo: BECS provides online book catalog browsing, customer checkout recording, inventory management, and promotion management through a standard web browser.
  Em escopo: Customer account registration and login
  Em escopo: Exact-title book search and catalog display
  Em escopo: Shopping cart and checkout
  Em escopo: Collection of card number during checkout without payment processing
  Em escopo: Receipt generation and purchase logging
  Em escopo: Member enrollment and promo-code usage
  Em escopo: Book, price, and stock management
  Em escopo: Low-stock email alerts
  Em escopo: Percentage-off promotion creation and member notification emails
  Fora de escopo: Real card payment authorization, capture, settlement, or money movement — deferred to a future phase
  Fora de escopo: Password recovery — explicitly excluded from the current scope
  Fora de escopo: Encryption requirements — explicitly not prioritized for the current scope
  Fora de escopo: Partial-title search — only exact title matching is required
  Fora de escopo: Author-based search — explicitly excluded from the current scope
  Fora de escopo: Multiple manager roles — the store has one manager
  Fora de escopo: Multiple copies of the same book in an order — prohibited by business policy
  Premissa: PA-01: Customers and the store manager have access to a standard web browser.
  Premissa: PA-02: An email delivery service is available for low-stock and promotion notifications. [INFERRED]
  Premissa: PA-03: Each book has a configurable low-stock threshold. [INFERRED]
  Restrição: REST-01 (Deployment): The system shall be accessible through a standard web browser.
  Restrição: REST-02 (Business): Only one store manager account shall exist.
  Restrição: REST-03 (Scope): The system shall not process actual payments or transfer money.
  Restrição: REST-04 (Scope): The system shall not provide password recovery.

Stakeholders:
  STK-01 - Customer (Usuário primário): Create an account, sign in, search available books, manage a cart, complete checkout, receive a receipt, and review purchase confirmation.
  STK-02 - Member (Usuário primário): Receive promotion notifications and apply eligible promo codes during checkout.
  STK-03 - Store Manager (Usuário primário): Manage books, prices, stock quantities, low-stock alerts, and percentage-off promotions.

Regras de negócio:
  RN-001 - Account registration without verification: Any site visitor may create a customer account without an identity-verification process.
  RN-002 - Exact-title search: Books are searchable only by an exact match of the book title; partial-title and author searches are not supported.
  RN-003 - Member promotion eligibility: Only members are eligible to use promo codes during checkout.
  RN-004 - One copy per book per order: An order may contain no more than one copy of each book.
  RN-005 - Low-stock alert exception: A low-stock notification is sent when stock reaches or falls below the configured low-stock threshold, except for books whose alerts have been disabled.
  RN-006 - Promotion type and notification: A promotion is expressed as a percentage discount and is communicated to all members when created.
  RN-007 - Payment-processing exclusion: Checkout collects a card number but does not authorize cards, process payments, or transfer money.
  RN-008 - Exclusive account roles: A store manager account and a regular customer account are mutually exclusive, and only one store manager account exists.

Requisitos funcionais:
  RF-001 - Register customer account: The system shall register a customer account without requiring identity verification. [Must have]
  RF-002 - Authenticate customer: The system shall authenticate a customer using registered account credentials. [Must have]
  RF-003 - Enroll member: The system shall enroll a customer as a member for promotion notifications. [Should have]
  RF-004 - Search books by exact title: The system shall return available books whose title exactly matches the submitted search title. [Must have]
  RF-005 - Display book details: The system shall display the title, author, and price for each book returned by a search. [Must have]
  RF-006 - Add book to cart: The system shall add a selected book to the customer's shopping cart. [Must have]
  RF-007 - Enforce single-copy limit: The system shall restrict each book to a quantity of one in a shopping cart. [Must have]
  RF-008 - Collect card number: The system shall collect a card number as checkout input without submitting it for payment authorization. [Must have]
  RF-009 - Apply promo code: The system shall apply a valid promo code to a member's checkout total. [Should have]
  RF-010 - Generate receipt: The system shall generate a receipt after a checkout is completed. [Must have]
  RF-011 - Record purchase: The system shall record the purchased books, purchasing customer, and purchase date and time after checkout completion. [Must have]
  RF-012 - Authenticate store manager: The system shall authenticate the store manager through a manager account distinct from customer accounts. [Must have]
  RF-013 - Add book: The system shall allow the store manager to add a book to the catalog. [Must have]
  RF-014 - Update book price: The system shall allow the store manager to update a book price. [Must have]
  RF-015 - View stock quantity: The system shall display the current stock quantity for each catalog book to the store manager. [Must have]
  RF-016 - Update stock quantity: The system shall allow the store manager to update a book's stock quantity. [INFERRED] [Must have]
  RF-017 - Suppress low-stock alert: The system shall allow the store manager to disable low-stock alerts for an individual book. [Should have]
  RF-018 - Send low-stock alert: The system shall email the store manager when an alert-enabled book reaches or falls below its configured low-stock threshold. [Should have]
  RF-019 - Create percentage promotion: The system shall allow the store manager to create a promotion with a percentage discount. [Should have]
  RF-020 - Notify members about promotion: The system shall email every enrolled member when the store manager creates a promotion. [Should have]

Requisitos não funcionais:
  RNF-001 (Compatibility) - The system shall support successful execution of registration, search, cart, checkout, and manager inventory functions in the two most recent major versions of Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari. [TBD] | Métrica: 100% of the five listed critical functions pass on each supported browser version. [TBD]
  RNF-002 (Performance Efficiency) - The system shall return exact-title search results within 2 seconds at the 95th percentile under 50 concurrent users. [TBD] | Métrica: Search response time is less than or equal to 2 seconds at the 95th percentile under 50 concurrent users. [TBD]
  RNF-003 (Reliability) - The system shall maintain monthly availability of at least 99.0%, excluding planned maintenance. [TBD] | Métrica: Monthly availability is greater than or equal to 99.0%. [TBD]
  RNF-004 (Reliability) - The system shall retain 100% of completed purchase records containing books, customer, and timestamp after a completed checkout. [TBD] | Métrica: 100% of 100 completed checkout test transactions have a corresponding complete purchase record. [TBD]

Histórias de usuário:
  HU-001 - Como a site visitor, quero create a customer account, para access the book-purchasing functions.
  HU-002 - Como a registered customer, quero search for a book by its exact title, para find books available for purchase.
  HU-003 - Como a registered customer, quero add a book to my cart, para prepare my order for checkout.
  HU-004 - Como a registered customer, quero complete checkout and receive a receipt, para have evidence that my purchase was recorded.
  HU-005 - Como a customer, quero enroll as a member, para receive promotion notifications.
  HU-006 - Como a member, quero apply a promo code during checkout, para receive the eligible percentage discount.
  HU-007 - Como the store manager, quero add books and maintain their prices and stock, para keep the catalog available for online sales.
  HU-008 - Como the store manager, quero receive low-stock notifications, para replenish books before inventory is exhausted.
  HU-009 - Como the store manager, quero create a percentage-off promotion, para inform members about promotional offers.

Casos de uso:
  UC-001 - Register customer account | Ator: Site Visitor
    1. The visitor opens the account-registration form.
    2. The visitor submits the required account information.
    3. The system creates the customer account without an identity-verification step.
    4. The system confirms successful registration.
  UC-002 - Search catalog by exact title | Ator: Registered Customer
    1. The customer enters a book title.
    2. The customer submits the search.
    3. The system searches for an exact title match.
    4. The system displays each matching book's title, author, and price.
  UC-003 - Add book to cart | Ator: Registered Customer
    1. The customer selects a displayed book.
    2. The customer requests to add the book to the cart.
    3. The system adds one copy of the book to the cart.
    4. The system displays the updated cart.
  UC-004 - Complete checkout | Ator: Registered Customer
    1. The customer opens checkout.
    2. The customer enters a card number.
    3. The customer confirms checkout.
    4. The system records the purchased books, customer, and timestamp without processing a payment.
    5. The system generates a receipt.
  UC-005 - Enroll as member | Ator: Customer
    1. The customer requests membership enrollment.
    2. The system records the customer as a member.
    3. The system confirms membership enrollment.
  UC-006 - Manage book inventory | Ator: Store Manager
    1. The store manager opens inventory management.
    2. The system displays catalog books and current stock quantities.
    3. The store manager adds a book or selects a book record.
    4. The store manager submits a price or stock-quantity update.
    5. The system stores the submitted inventory change.
  UC-007 - Create promotion | Ator: Store Manager
    1. The store manager opens promotion management.
    2. The store manager enters a percentage discount.
    3. The store manager creates the promotion.
    4. The system stores the promotion.
    5. The system emails the promotion to all enrolled members.

Critérios de aceite:
  CA-001 - Dado a site visitor is not authenticated, quando the visitor submits valid registration information, então the system creates a customer account without displaying or requiring an identity-verification step.
  CA-002 - Dado a customer account exists, quando the customer submits its registered credentials, então the system creates an authenticated customer session.
  CA-003 - Dado an authenticated customer is not a member, quando the customer requests membership enrollment, então the system records the customer with member status.
  CA-004 - Dado an available book has the title "Example Book", quando a customer searches for "Example Book", então the system returns the book; a search for "Example" returns zero results unless a book title exactly equals "Example".
  CA-005 - Dado a search returns a book, quando the system displays the search results, então each returned book displays one title, one author, and one price.
  CA-006 - Dado an authenticated customer views an available book not in the cart, quando the customer adds the book to the cart, então the cart displays the selected book with quantity 1.
  CA-007 - Dado a customer's cart already contains one copy of a book, quando the customer attempts to add the same book again, então the cart retains a quantity of exactly 1 for that book.
  CA-008 - Dado an authenticated customer has a non-empty cart, quando the customer submits a card number during checkout, então the system accepts the card number as checkout input and creates no payment-authorization, payment-capture, or money-transfer transaction.
  CA-009 - Dado an authenticated member has a valid promo code and a non-empty cart, quando the member submits the promo code at checkout, então the checkout total reflects the promotion's configured percentage discount.
  CA-010 - Dado a customer completes checkout, quando the system records the purchase, então the system generates one receipt for that checkout.
  CA-011 - Dado a customer completes checkout containing one or more books, quando the checkout is completed, então the system stores a purchase record containing the purchased books, customer identifier, and completion timestamp.
  CA-012 - Dado a manager account exists, quando an account is designated as the manager account, então the system prevents that account from being registered or used as a regular customer account.
  CA-013 - Dado the store manager is authenticated, quando the manager submits a new book record, então the system adds the submitted book to the catalog.
  CA-014 - Dado the store manager is authenticated and a catalog book exists, quando the manager submits a new price for the book, então the system displays the submitted price for that book.
  CA-015 - Dado the store manager is authenticated and a catalog book has stock quantity 7, quando the manager views inventory, então the system displays stock quantity 7 for that book.
  CA-016 - Dado the store manager is authenticated and a catalog book exists, quando the manager submits stock quantity 12, então the system stores and displays stock quantity 12 for that book.
  CA-017 - Dado the store manager is authenticated and a book has low-stock alerts enabled, quando the manager disables low-stock alerts for the book, então the system records low-stock alerts as disabled for that book.
  CA-018 - Dado an alert-enabled book has a configured low-stock threshold of 3 and its stock changes from 4 to 3, quando the system records the stock quantity, então the system sends one low-stock email to the store manager.
  CA-019 - Dado the store manager is authenticated, quando the manager creates a promotion with a 15% discount, então the system stores a promotion with a percentage discount value of 15.
  CA-020 - Dado two customers are enrolled as members, quando the store manager creates a promotion, então the system sends one promotion email to each of the two members.

Glossário:
  Customer: A registered regular user who can browse books, use a cart, and complete checkout.
  Member: A customer enrolled to receive promotion notifications and eligible to use promo codes.
  Store Manager: The single account holder responsible for catalog, inventory, low-stock alert, and promotion management.
  Exact-title search: A search that returns a book only when the submitted title equals the complete stored book title.
  Promo code: A code associated with a percentage-off promotion that may be applied only by a member during checkout.
  Low-stock threshold: The stock quantity at or below which an alert-enabled book triggers a notification to the store manager.
  Checkout: The process that records a customer's requested purchase and generates a receipt without processing a real payment.
  Receipt: The system-generated evidence that a checkout was completed and recorded.

When old requirements don’t exist
Most older systems do not have documented—let alone accurate—requirements. In the absence of 
reliable documentation, teams might reverse-engineer an understanding of what the system does 
from the user interfaces, code, and database. We think of this as “software archaeology.” To maximize 
the benefit from reverse engineering, the archaeology expedition should record what it learns in 
the form of requirements and design descriptions. Accumulating accurate information about certain 
portions of the current system positions the team to enhance a system with low risk, to replace a 
system without missing critical functionality, and to perform future enhancements efficiently. It halts 
the knowledge drain, so future maintainers better understand the changes that were just made.
If updating the requirements is overly burdensome, it will fall by the wayside as busy people rush 
on to the next change request. Obsolete requirements aren’t helpful for future enhancements. There’s 
a widespread fear in the software industry that writing documentation will consume too much time; 
the knee-jerk reaction is to neglect all opportunities to update requirements documentation. But 
what’s the cost if you don’t update the requirements and a future maintainer (perhaps you!) has to 
regenerate that information? The answer to this question will let you make a thoughtful business 
decision concerning whether to revise the requirements documentation when you change or 
re-create the software.
When the team performs additional enhancements and maintenance over time, it can extend 
these fractional knowledge representations, steadily improving the system documentation. The 
incremental cost of recording this newly found knowledge is small compared with the cost of 
someone having to rediscover it later on. Implementing enhancements almost always necessitates 
further requirements development, so add those new requirements to an existing requirements 
repository, if there is one. If you’re replacing an old system, you have an opportunity to document 
the requirements for the new one and to keep the requirements up to date with what you learn 
throughout the project. Try to leave the requirements in better shape than you found them.
Which requirements should you specify?
It’s not always worth taking the time to generate a complete set of requirements for an entire 
production system. Many options lie between the two extremes of continuing forever with no 
requirements documentation and reconstructing a perfect requirements set. Knowing why you’d like 
to have written requirements available lets you judge whether the cost of rebuilding all—or even 
part—of the specification is a sound investment.

4.1 DoRCU Methodology
DoRCU, according to Griselda Báez & Barba Brunner ( 2001), has been developed in an 
academic environment and validated in a project during a public health context in Cuba. It is 
called DoRCU for Documentation of User-Centered Requirements. The article presents the 
following characteristics (Griselda Báez & Barba Brunner, 2001): (i) it consists of 4 stages: 
elicitation, analysis, specification and validation and certification of requirements; (ii) it describes 
an iterative process; (iii) it involves high user participation in all its stages; (iv) it prioritizes the 
satisfaction of user needs; and (v) it is adaptable to other models (flexibility). Fig. 2 shows a

Trace Data
Requirements trace data for existing systems will help the enhancement developer determine 
which components she might have to modify because of a change in a specific requirement. In an 
ideal world, when you’re replacing a system, the existing system would have a full set of functional 
requirements such that you could establish traceability between the old and new systems to 
avoid overlooking any requirements. However, a poorly documented old system won’t have trace 
information available, and establishing rigorous traceability for both existing and new systems is time 
consuming.
As with any new development, it’s a good practice to create a traceability matrix to link the new 
or changed requirements to the corresponding design elements, code, and test cases. Accumulating 
trace links as you perform the development work takes little effort, whereas it’s a great deal of work 
to regenerate the links from a completed system. For replacement systems, perform requirements 
tracing at a high level: make a list of features and user stories for the existing system and prioritize 
to determine which of those will be implemented in the new system. See Chapter 29, “Links in the 
requirements chain,” for more information on tracing requirements.
How to discover the requirements of an existing system
In enhancement and replacement projects, even if you don’t have existing documentation, you do 
have a system to work from to discover the relevant requirements. During enhancement projects, 
consider drawing a dialog map for the new screens you have to add, showing the navigation 
connections to and from existing display elements. You might write use cases or user stories that span 
the new and existing functionality.
In replacement system projects, you need to understand all of the desired functionality, just as 
you do on any new development project. Study the user interface of the existing system to identify 
candidate functionality for the new system. Examine existing system interfaces to determine what 
data is exchanged between systems today. Understand how users use the current system. If no one 
understands the functionality and business rules behind the user interface, someone will need to look 
at the code or database to understand what’s going on. Analyze any documentation that does 
exist—design documents, help screens, user manuals, training materials—to identify requirements.
You might not need to specify functional requirements for the existing system at all, instead 
creating models to fill the information void. Swimlane diagrams can describe how users do their jobs 
with the system today. Context diagrams, data flow diagrams, and entity-relationship diagrams are 
also useful. You might create user requirements, specifying them only at a high level without filling 
in all of the details. Another way to begin closing the information gap is to create data dictionary 
entries when you add new data elements to the system and modify existing definitions. The test suite 
might be useful as an initial source of information to recover the software requirements, because tests 
represent an alternative view of requirements.CHAPTER 21 Enhancement and replacement projects 401
Sometimes “good enough” is enough
A third-party assessment of current business analysis practices in one organization revealed 
that their teams did a fairly good job of writing requirements for new projects, but they failed 
to update the requirements as the products evolved through a series of enhancement releases. 
The BAs did create requirements for each enhancement project. However, they did not merge 
all of those revisions back into the requirements baseline. The organization’s manager couldn’t 
think of a measurable benefit from keeping the existing documentation 100 percent updated 
to reflect the implemented systems. He assumed that his requirements always reflected only 
80 to 90 percent of the working software anyway, so there was little value in trying to perfect 
the requirements for an enhancement.

Base: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §9.6 · IEEE 830-1998 §3 · Sommerville (2016, cap. 4)
O Documento de Especificação de Requisitos de Software (SRS) é o contrato técnico que descreve o 
que o sistema deve fazer e sob quais condições de qualidade. Ele serve de referência para 
desenvolvedores, testadores, gerentes e clientes durante todo o ciclo de vida do projeto.
1.1 Artefatos Obrigatórios e sua Ordem
Um SRS completo e formal deve conter os seguintes artefatos, nesta ordem:
• ESCOPO: Define o que está DENTRO e FORA do projeto. Evita scope creep.
• STAKEHOLDERS: Lista todos os envolvidos: quem usa, quem financia, quem é afetado.
• PREMISSAS E RESTRIÇÕES: Fatos assumidos como verdadeiros e limites impostos ao projeto.
• REGRAS DE NEGÓCIO (RN): Políticas, fórmulas e condições de negócio que existem independentemente 
do software.
• REQUISITOS FUNCIONAIS (RF): O que o sistema DEVE FAZER — comportamentos, serviços, respostas a 
entradas.
• REQUISITOS NÃO FUNCIONAIS (RNF): Como o sistema deve SER — atributos de qualidade 
quantificáveis.
• HISTÓRIAS DE USUÁRIO (HU): Necessidades na perspectiva do usuário: Como [perfil], quero [ação], para
[benefício].
• CASOS DE USO (UC): Interações detalhadas ator-sistema com fluxo principal, alternativo e exceções.
• CRITÉRIOS DE ACEITE (CA): Condições testáveis em formato BDD (Dado/Quando/Então) que definem 
quando o requisito está concluído.
• GLOSSÁRIO: Termos do domínio com definição precisa para eliminar ambiguidades.
1.2 Como os Artefatos se Interconectam
Os artefatos formam uma cadeia de rastreabilidade. Cada RF deve ter origem em um STK 
(stakeholder) ou RN. Cada HU deve ter pelo menos um RF associado. Cada RF e HU devem ter pelo menos um CA. Esta rastreabilidade garante que nada seja implementado sem justificativa de 
negócio e que tudo que foi prometido seja testável.

the requirements for the new one and to keep the requirements up to date with what you learn

Which requirements should you specify?
It’s not always worth taking the time to generate a complete set of requirements for an entire 
production system. Many options lie between the two extremes of continuing forever with no 
requirements documentation and reconstructing a perfect requirements set. Knowing why you’d like 
to have written requirements available lets you judge whether the cost of rebuilding all—or even 
part—of the specification is a sound investment.
Perhaps your current system is a shapeless mass of history and mystery like the one in Figure 21-2. 
Imagine that you’ve been asked to implement some new functionality in region A in this figure. 
Begin by recording the new requirements in a structured SRS or in a requirements management tool. 
When you add the new functionality, you’ll have to figure out how it interfaces to or fits in with the 
existing system. The bridges in Figure 21-2 between region A and your current system represent these 
interfaces. This analysis provides insight into the white portion of the current system, region B. In 
addition to the requirements for region A, this insight is the new knowledge you need to capture.CHAPTER 21 Enhancement and replacement projects 399

Rarely do you need to document the entire existing system. Focus detailed requirements efforts 
on the changes needed to meet the business objectives. If you’re replacing a system, start by 
documenting the areas prioritized as most important to achieve the business objectives or those that 
pose the highest implementation risk. Any new requirements identified during the gap analysis will 
need to be specified at the same level of precision and using the same techniques as you would for a 
new system.
Level of detail
One of the biggest challenges is determining the appropriate level of detail at which to document 
requirements gleaned from the existing system. For enhancements, defining requirements for the 
new functionality alone might be sufficient. However, you will usually benefit from documenting all of 
the functionality that closely relates to the enhancement, to ensure that the change fits in seamlessly 
(region B in Figure 21-2). You might want to create business processes, user requirements, and/or 
functional requirements for those related areas. For example, let’s say you are adding a discount code 
feature to an existing shopping cart function, but you don’t have any documented requirements for 
the shopping cart. You might be tempted to write just a single user story: “As a customer, I need to be 
able to enter a discount code so I can get the cheapest price for the product.” However, this user story 
alone lacks context, so consider capturing other user stories about shopping cart operations. That 
information could be valuable the next time you need to modify the shopping cart function.
I worked with one team that was just beginning to develop the requirements for version 2 of 
a major product with embedded software. They hadn’t done a good job on the requirements for 
version 1, which was currently being implemented. The lead BA wondered, “Is it worth going back 
to improve the SRS for version 1?” The company anticipated that this product line would be a major 
revenue generator for at least 10 years. They also planned to reuse some of the core requirements 
in several spin-off products. In this case, it made sense to improve the requirements documentation 
for version 1 because it was the foundation for all subsequent development work in this product line.

Most of this book describes requirements development as though you are beginning a new software 
or system development project, sometimes called a green-field project. However, many organizations 
devote much of their effort to enhancing or replacing existing information systems or building 
new releases of established commercial products. Most of the practices described in this book are 
appropriate for enhancement and replacement projects. This chapter provides specific suggestions as 
to which practices are most relevant and how to use them.
An enhancement project is one in which new capabilities are added to an existing system. 
Enhancement projects might also involve correcting defects, adding new reports, and modifying 
functionality to comply with revised business rules or needs.
A replacement (or reengineering) project replaces an existing application with a new custom-built 
system, a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) system, or a hybrid of those. Replacement projects are 
most commonly implemented to improve performance, cut costs (such as maintenance costs or 
license fees), take advantage of modern technologies, or meet regulatory requirements. If your 
replacement project will involve a COTS solution, the guidance presented in Chapter 22, “Packaged 
solution projects,” will also be helpful.

claim that a small enhancement doesn’t warrant writing any requirements. Developers might believe 
that they don’t need detailed requirements if they are replacing an existing system’s functionality. 
The approaches described in this chapter can help you to deal with the challenges of enhancing or 
replacing an existing system to improve its ability to meet the organization’s current business needs.

GABARITO — Project Scenario 8: BECS (Book E-Commerce System)
Use: "ground_truth" field for RAGAS (context_precision / context_recall).
Each line is an atomic, checkable claim against the scenario text and the
knowledge base — not a full SRS, just the set of facts a well-grounded SRS
for this scenario should be able to cover.

- Any visitor can create an account with no verification process.
- Logged-in users can search for books by title only, with an exact match (no partial matches, no search by author).
- Users can view a book's title, author, and price, add it to a cart, and check out.
- Only one copy of each book can be purchased per order.
- Members (a subset of registered users) can apply promo codes at checkout.
- The manager (a single login-based account) can add books, edit prices, and view stock levels.
- The system must automatically notify the manager by email when a book's stock is low, unless notifications are disabled for that specific book.
- The manager can create percentage-off promotions; creating one automatically emails all members.
- The system does not process real credit card payments; it only collects a card number, produces a receipt, and logs the purchase (item, buyer, timestamp).
- Encryption and password recovery are explicitly out of scope for this version.
- There is only one manager account; no multi-manager roles are needed.
- A manager account must never also be a regular customer account.
- The system must run as a normal browser-accessible web application, with no exotic technical requirements.

em_escopo: Account creation for any visitor, with no verification process
Book search by exact title match (logged-in users)
Viewing book title, author, and price
Shopping cart with a limit of one copy per book per order
Checkout flow that collects a card number, generates a receipt, and logs the purchase
Member signup to receive promotion notifications and use promo codes at checkout
Manager login to manage inventory (add books, edit prices, view stock)
Automatic low-stock email alert to the manager, with per-book opt-out
Manager-created percentage-off promotions with automatic email to all members
fora_de_escopo: Real credit card / payment processing — deferred to a later phase
Encryption — not a priority for this version
Password recovery — not a priority for this version
Multiple manager accounts or manager roles — only one manager
Partial/fuzzy search or search by author — title search is exact-match only
Multiple copies of the same book per order — limited to one
premissas: PA-01: Only one person will operate the manager account for the store.
restricoes: REST-01 (Tecnica): The system must be usable through a normal web browser, with no exotic client-side requirements.

stakeholders.descricao: Store Manager — the single account responsible for managing inventory (add books, edit prices, view stock) and creating promotions; must never also be a regular customer account.
Visitor — anyone arriving at the site who can create an account with no verification process.
Registered User / Customer — logged-in user who can search for books, add them to a cart, and check out.
Member — a registered user who opted in to promotion notifications; the only type of user who can apply promo codes at checkout.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: A cart may contain at most one copy of each distinct book per order.
A manager account must never also function as a regular customer account.
Only members (not all registered users) can apply promo codes at checkout.
The low-stock email alert to the manager is suppressed for a given book if the manager has disabled notifications for that specific book.
Creating a new percentage-off promotion automatically triggers an email to all members.

requisitos_funcionais.descricao: The system must allow any visitor to create an account with no verification process.
The system must allow logged-in users to search for books by title using an exact match only (no partial match, no search by author).
The system must display each book's title, author, and price.
The system must allow users to add a book to their shopping cart.
The system must prevent a user from adding more than one copy of the same book to their cart in a single order.
The system must allow users to complete checkout for the items in their cart.
The system must allow a registered user to sign up as a member to receive promotion notifications.
The system must allow members to apply a promo code during checkout.
The system must provide a login for the manager, separate from customer accounts.
The system must allow the manager to add new books to the inventory.
The system must allow the manager to edit the price of existing books.
The system must allow the manager to view current stock levels.
The system must send an email notification to the manager when a book's stock is low, unless notifications are disabled for that book.
The system must allow the manager to create percentage-off promotions.
The system must automatically email all members when a new promotion is created.
The system must collect a card number during checkout without processing an actual payment.
The system must generate a receipt after checkout.
The system must log each purchase, including the item, the buyer, and the timestamp.

requisitos_nao_funcionais.descricao: The system must be usable through a standard web browser, with no exotic or non-standard client-side requirements.

historias_de_usuario.descricao: As a visitor, I want to create an account with no verification process, so that I can start using the site quickly.
As a registered user, I want to search for a book by its exact title, so that I can find the book I'm looking for.
As a registered user, I want to view a book's title, author, and price, so that I can decide whether to buy it.
As a registered user, I want to add a book to my cart, so that I can purchase it later.
As a registered user, I want to check out my cart, so that I can complete my purchase.
As a member, I want to apply a promo code at checkout, so that I can get a discount.
As the manager, I want to add new books and edit their prices, so that I can keep the catalog up to date.
As the manager, I want to be notified when a book's stock is low, so that I can restock in time.
As the manager, I want to create percentage-off promotions, so that I can attract more sales.
As a member, I want to receive an email when a new promotion is created, so that I know about current deals.

casos_de_uso.descricao: Search and Purchase Book — a logged-in user searches for a book by exact title, adds it to the cart, and completes checkout.
Manage Inventory — the manager logs in and adds new books, edits prices, or views current stock levels.
Create Promotion — the manager creates a percentage-off promotion, and the system automatically emails all members.

criterios_de_aceite.descricao: Given a logged-in user, when they search for a book title that exactly matches an existing book, then the system returns that book with its title, author, and price.
Given a user already has one copy of a book in their cart, when they try to add another copy of the same book, then the system prevents the second copy from being added.
Given a member is at checkout with a valid promo code, when they apply the code, then the system applies the corresponding discount.
Given a book's stock drops below the defined threshold and notifications are enabled for that book, when the stock update occurs, then the system sends an email to the manager.
Given the manager creates a new percentage-off promotion, when the promotion is saved, then the system automatically sends an email to all members.
